newsitem.title: UK: Asda shares fall on Welcome Break bid.
newsitem.headline: Asda shares fall on Welcome Break bid.

text.p: Shares in Asda Plc fell on Friday on reports that it had bid for Granada Group's Welcome Break motorway service areas, causing fears that diversification could leave Asda's direction unclear, traders said.
Shares in the supermarket chain were down 1-3/4p at 113 by 0924 GMT.
Both Asda and Granada declined to make any immediate comment on an article in the Financial Times on Friday which named Asda named as one of four bidders for the Welcome Break chain.
"It would not be commercially sensible for us to comment on the disposal at this time," a Granada spokesman said.
But industry sources say they expect the sale of Welcome Break to come sooner rather than later, perhaps even as soon as within the next three weeks.
The Financial Times said offers for Welcome Break are believed to be for at least 400 million stg.
"Food retail shares are traditionally weak when there's any consideration of diversification," Credit Lyonnais Laing analyst Paul Smiddy said.
"If Asda were to make an offer for Welcome there may be some concern over the direction of the company," he added.
